Omnipresent

om-nih-PREZ-ent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Omnipresent is present everywhere at the same time.

By the mid-2010s, smartphones had become nearly omnipresent, showing up in the hands of commuters, students, and toddlers alike.

Worked Example

Security cameras felt almost omnipresent in the new terminal, mounted on every pillar and above every gate.

Seeming to exist or appear absolutely everywhere at once is exactly what omnipresent describes.

How Omnipresent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ever-present

ever-present: existing or appearing at all times or places

all-pervading

all-pervading: spreading through and existing in every part of something

Antonyms

rare

rare: not found or occurring often

isolated

isolated: occurring alone; separate from others

How Strong Is It? — ever-present → omnipresent → all-pervading

ever-present vs. omnipresent

ever-present vs. omnipresent: Ever-present is weaker than omnipresent: a refrigerator's hum is ever-present in one kitchen, while something omnipresent exists everywhere at once, in every place at the same time.

all-pervading vs. omnipresent

all-pervading vs. omnipresent: All-pervading is more intense than omnipresent: an omnipresent thing is found everywhere, but an all-pervading smell goes further, soaking into every corner and fiber of every room.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — omni-

Prefix — omni-: all (Latin)

Root — present

Root — present: being present, at hand (from Latin praesens, 'being present')

Put it together

Put it together: Omnipresent combines the Latin prefix omni- ('all') with present ('being present, at hand,' from Latin praesens). Something omnipresent is, quite literally, present in all places.
